title: Scheduler probe amplification caused transient p95 regressions
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: During a controlled config rollout of a scheduler probing heuristic, probe traffic amplified under a bursty capacity event and caused transient p95/p99 latency regressions for generation workloads. This ticket tracks the follow-up actions, mitigations applied during the incident, and long-term safeguards to prevent recurrence.
impact: Impacted hosted customers in us-west1 and us-east1 on models with sequence lengths >2048. Synthetic p95 increased from baseline ~120ms to ~420ms for affected model variants for ~45 minutes. No data loss. Several high-throughput customers observed increased tail latency and started fallback behavior to older model variants.

root_cause: The new probing heuristic increased probe frequency without sufficient backoff/jitter during pool churn. When GPUs were recycled during autoscale, the scheduler aggressively probed execution paths (kernel variants and attention implementations) to re-evaluate performance. Probe bursts coincided across many pods, causing transient overload on kernel-selection paths and increased queueing. Two contributing factors: (1) probe rate was proportional to active request volume and lacked global coordinating limits; (2) probes used synchronous microbenchmarks that occupied execution resources and interfered with live inference queues.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of probing heuristic to v2.0 (implemented 2026-02-24 10:23 UTC)
Applied temporary rate limit on probe launches in scheduler (config: max_probes_per_node=2)
Enabled probe jitter and randomized backoff for canary nodes
Added alert: probe_rate_per_node > 1/min for >5m triggers P0 alert
action_items: ENG-711208: Implement centralized probe throttler that enforces global concurrent probe limits across a pool (owner: Ethan Morales, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-10)

ENG-711210: Add canary gating: probe intensity only increases after KV cache warmup and steady-state throughput for 10 minutes (owner: Carlos Ruiz, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-08)
ENG-711211: Create e2e regression test that simulates autoscale churn + probe bursts and fails the build if p95 deviates >25% from baseline (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-711212: Dashboard telemetry: per-node probe rate, per-model probe failures, and probe-induced CPU/GPU utilization graphs (owner: Observability Team, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-711213: Documentation: update scheduling playbook with probe safety knobs and rollback steps; include runbook snippets for oncall (owner: Support Docs, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-05)
Longer term: Evaluate probe-free heuristics (model tagging + historical performance lookup) to reduce live probing frequency (owner: Research/Applied ML, due: 2026-Q2)
